```{r}
#| label: setup

# Packages ----------------------------------------------------------------
library(haven)    # read SPSS .sav files
library(dplyr)    # data wrangling
library(tidyr)    # reshaping
library(ggplot2)  # charts
library(knitr)    # tables
library(car)      # Levene's test

# Data: instructor-provided cleaned file (Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav) ---------
# Keep the .sav file in the same folder as this .qmd file
efcu <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav")

# Grouping variable for R4 (Q38: 1 = Yes, lives in HQ area; 2 = No)
efcu <- efcu |>
  mutate(
    residence = factor(as.numeric(q38), levels = 1:2,
                       labels = c("HQ area", "Elsewhere")),
    # Q12rc: per Case Exhibit 31.2, code 3 = "No answer" -> treated as missing
    q12rc = ifelse(as.numeric(q12) == 3, NA, as.numeric(q12))
  )

# Helper 1: frequency table with valid percentages ------------------------
freq_tbl <- function(x, labels) {
  x <- factor(as.numeric(x), levels = seq_along(labels), labels = labels)
  tibble(Response = levels(x),
         n = as.vector(table(x))) |>
    mutate(`Valid %` = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
}

# Helper 2: one-sample t-test summary row ---------------------------------
t_row <- function(x, mu, item) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  r <- t.test(x, mu = mu)
  tibble(Item = item,
         n = sum(!is.na(x)),
         Mean = round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
         SD = round(sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
         `Test value` = mu,
         t = round(unname(r$statistic), 2),
         df = round(unname(r$parameter), 1),
         p = format.pval(r$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001))
}

# Helper 3: independent-groups t-test summary row -------------------------
# Levene's test decides between the pooled (equal variances) and Welch t-test
ind_t_row <- function(x, group, item) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  lev_p <- leveneTest(x ~ group)$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  eq <- lev_p >= .05
  r <- t.test(x ~ group, var.equal = eq)
  m <- tapply(x, group, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  s <- tapply(x, group, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(Item = item,
         `HQ area M (SD)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", m[1], s[1]),
         `Elsewhere M (SD)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", m[2], s[2]),
         `Levene p` = round(lev_p, 3),
         Test = ifelse(eq, "Pooled", "Welch"),
         t = round(unname(r$statistic), 2),
         df = round(unname(r$parameter), 1),
         p = format.pval(r$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001))
}

# Helper 4: chi-square test of independence summary row -------------------
# Fisher's exact test is added because several cells have expected counts < 5
chi_row <- function(x, group, item) {
  tb <- table(group, as.numeric(x))
  r <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tb, correct = FALSE))
  tibble(Item = item,
         `Chi-square` = round(unname(r$statistic), 2),
         df = unname(r$parameter),
         p = format.pval(r$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001),
         `Min. expected` = round(min(r$expected), 1),
         `Fisher p` = format.pval(fisher.test(tb)$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001))
}

agree_labels <- c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Uncertain",
                  "Agree", "Strongly Agree")
```

# Research Questions & Analysis Plan

```{r}
#| label: tbl-plan
#| tbl-cap: "Data analysis table for R3, R6, R4a, R4b, and R4c"

tibble(
  RQ = c("R3", "R6", "R6", "R4a", "R4b", "R4c", "R4c"),
  `Research question` = c(
    "What are members' attitudes toward the proficiency of CU employees?",
    "How effectively is the credit union operated?", "",
    "Do HQ-area and other members differ in attitudes toward employee proficiency?",
    "Do HQ-area and other members differ in awareness of services?",
    "Do HQ-area and other members differ in views of operational effectiveness?", ""),
  Variables = c("Q3 – Q6; Att_employee",
                "Q9r, Q10r, Q31 – Q34, Q37r", "Q11, Q12rc",
                "Q38 (IV); Att_employee (DV)",
                "Q38 (IV); Q13r – Q26r (DV)",
                "Q38 (IV); Q9r, Q10r, Q31 – Q34, Q37r (DV)", "Q38 (IV); Q11, Q12rc (DV)"),
  Scale = c("Interval", "Interval", "Nominal", "Nominal; Interval",
            "Nominal; Ordinal", "Nominal; Interval", "Nominal; Nominal"),
  `Statistical test` = c(
    "Descriptive statistics, one-sample t-test",
    "Descriptive statistics, one-sample t-test",
    "Frequencies, chi-square goodness-of-fit test",
    "Descriptive statistics, independent-groups t-test",
    "Cross-tabulation, chi-square test of independence",
    "Descriptive statistics, independent-groups t-tests",
    "Cross-tabulation, chi-square test of independence")
) |>
  kable()
```

The sample has `r nrow(efcu)` credit union members: `r sum(efcu$residence == "HQ area")` live in the headquarters area and `r sum(efcu$residence == "Elsewhere")` live elsewhere. Following Case Exhibit 31.2, "No Opinion" and "No answer" responses are treated as missing, so all percentages are **valid percentages**.

**Measurement decisions from the previous activity.** The reliability and factor analysis showed that Q3 – Q6 form one reliable scale, so R3 and R4a use the composite **Att_employee** (the average of Q3 – Q6). The operations items in R6 and R4c did not form a reliable scale, so each item is analyzed on its own.

# R3: Attitudes Toward Employee Proficiency

## R3: Descriptive Statistics (Q3 – Q6)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement with statements about credit union employees (valid %)"

r3_items <- c(q3 = "Q3: Courteous", q4 = "Q4: Helpful",
              q5 = "Q5: Professional", q6 = "Q6: Always available")

r3_long <- efcu |>
  select(all_of(names(r3_items))) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "var", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(Item = r3_items[var],
         Response = factor(value, levels = 1:5, labels = agree_labels)) |>
  count(var, Item, Response, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(var, Item) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  ungroup()

r3_long |>
  select(Item, Response, pct) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Response, values_from = pct) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-r3
#| fig-cap: "Agreement with statements about credit union employees (Q3 – Q6)"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.5

r3_long |>
  mutate(Group = case_when(as.numeric(Response) >= 4 ~ "Agree",
                           as.numeric(Response) == 3 ~ "Uncertain",
                           TRUE ~ "Disagree"),
         Group = factor(Group, levels = c("Disagree", "Uncertain", "Agree"))) |>
  group_by(Item, Group) |>
  summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Item, y = pct, fill = Group)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(pct >= 5, paste0(pct, "%"), "")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Disagree = "#d6604d", Uncertain = "grey80",
                               Agree = "#4393c3")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "%", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## R3: One-Sample t-tests (Att_employee & Q3 – Q6)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3-t
#| tbl-cap: "One-sample t-tests for employee proficiency (test value = 3, Uncertain)"

bind_rows(
  t_row(efcu$Att_employee, 3, "Att_employee: Average of Q3 – Q6"),
  t_row(efcu$q3, 3, "Q3: Courteous"),
  t_row(efcu$q4, 3, "Q4: Helpful"),
  t_row(efcu$q5, 3, "Q5: Professional"),
  t_row(efcu$q6, 3, "Q6: Always available")
) |> kable()
```

## R3: Insight

**Insight.** Members hold their credit union employees in high regard. Almost nobody disagrees with any of the four statements, and agreement is highest for courtesy and helpfulness (@tbl-r3, @fig-r3). The overall attitude score averages 4.21 on the 5-point scale, well above "uncertain" (t(127) = 22.95, p < .001; @tbl-r3-t). Each statement on its own is also significantly positive. Professionalism (M = 4.08) and availability (M = 4.08) score slightly below courtesy (M = 4.35) and helpfulness (M = 4.31). Professionalism and availability each draw 18.0% "uncertain" answers, and availability is the only item with any disagreement (3.1%). Availability is therefore the one modest area to watch. Overall, employees are a clear **strength** of the credit union. Staff attitudes are not why members borrow elsewhere.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-gof
#| tbl-cap: "Chi-square goodness-of-fit tests for nominal items (equal proportions expected)"

gof_row <- function(x, k, item) {
  tb <- table(factor(as.numeric(x), levels = 1:k))
  r <- chisq.test(tb)
  tibble(Item = item,
         `Chi-square` = round(unname(r$statistic), 2),
         df = unname(r$parameter),
         p = format.pval(r$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001))
}

bind_rows(
  gof_row(efcu$q11,   2, "Q11: Statements easy to understand"),
  gof_row(efcu$q12rc, 2, "Q12rc: Accounts kept confidential")
) |> kable()
```

## R6: Insight

**Insight.** Members believe the credit union is run well. The day-to-day "back office" gets the highest marks. Overall, 84.3% rate management and operations as excellent or good (M = 4.07, t(120) = 16.12, p < .001; @tbl-r6-t). Statements are seen as accurate (M = 3.47 on a 4-point scale, p < .001). Almost everyone (97.7%) finds them easy to understand (χ²(1) = 116.28, p < .001; @tbl-r6-q11, @tbl-r6-gof). Members also agree that personnel keep financial information confidential (78.1% agree; M = 3.95, p < .001; @fig-r6).

Three areas need attention:

- **Loan processes are rated lowest.** Only 57.8% agree that loan applications are simple and easy, and 60.2% that loans are processed promptly. Both are still above neutral (p < .001), but this fits the R2 finding from the previous report that members see no loan rate advantage here.
- **Statements may come too rarely.** 22.7% of members say statements come "not often enough," so frequency falls short of the "about right" ideal (M = 2.77, t(127) = −6.10, p < .001).
- **Confidentiality is not universal.** Among members who answered, 69.8% say their accounts are kept confidential, but almost a third (30.2%) say they are not (χ²(1) = 16.64, p < .001; @tbl-r6-q12). Another 22 members gave no answer.

# R4: Headquarters Area vs. Elsewhere

## R4a: Independent-Groups t-test (Att_employee)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4a-t
#| tbl-cap: "Independent-groups t-test: attitude toward employee proficiency by residence"

kable(ind_t_row(efcu$Att_employee, efcu$residence,
                "Att_employee: Average of Q3 – Q6"))
```

## R4a: Insight

**Insight.** Members feel the same way about employees wherever they live. Both groups rate staff very positively. Members in the headquarters area score slightly higher (M = 4.28) than those elsewhere (M = 4.14), but the gap is small and not significant (t(126) = 1.29, p = .198; @tbl-r4a-t, @fig-r4a). Members living away from headquarters do **not** feel that employees are less courteous, helpful, professional, or available to them. The strength found in R3 holds for all members.

## R4b: Cross-Tabulation (Awareness of Services by Residence)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b
#| tbl-cap: "Awareness of credit union services by residence (row % within each group)"

aware_items <- c(
  q13_r = "Regular share account",       q14_r = "Special subaccounts",
  q15_r = "Christmas club account",      q16_r = "Individual Retirement Account",
  q17_r = "MasterCard credit card",      q18_r = "Signature loans",
  q19_r = "New car loans",               q20_r = "Late model car loans",
  q21_r = "Older model car loans",       q22_r = "Household goods/appliance loans",
  q23_r = "Recreational loans",          q24_r = "Share collateralized loans",
  q25_r = "IRA loans",                   q26_r = "Line of credit loans")

aware_labels <- c("Unaware", "Aware, not used", "Aware & used")

r4b_long <- efcu |>
  select(residence, all_of(names(aware_items))) |>
  mutate(across(-residence, as.numeric)) |>
  pivot_longer(-residence, names_to = "var", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(Service = aware_items[var],
         Response = factor(value, levels = 1:3, labels = aware_labels)) |>
  count(var, Service, residence, Response, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(var, Service, residence) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  ungroup()

r4b_long |>
  mutate(col = paste0(residence, ": ", Response)) |>
  select(var, Service, col, pct) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = pct) |>
  mutate(Item = paste0(toupper(sub("_r", "", var)), "r")) |>
  select(Item, Service, starts_with("HQ"), starts_with("Else")) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}

#| fig-cap: "Percent of members who have used each service, by residence"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

r4b_long |>
  filter(Response == "Aware & used") |>
  mutate(Service = reorder(Service, pct)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Service, y = pct, fill = residence)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("HQ area" = "steelblue", "Elsewhere" = "darkorange")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% aware and have used", fill = NULL) +
```

## R4b: Chi-square Tests of Independence (Q13r – Q26r)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b-chi
#| tbl-cap: "Chi-square tests of independence: awareness of services by residence"

bind_rows(lapply(names(aware_items), function(v)
  chi_row(efcu[[v]], efcu$residence,
          paste0(toupper(sub("_r", "", v)), "r: ", aware_items[v])))) |>
  kable()
```

Several services have cells with expected counts below 5, so Fisher's exact test is shown as a check. It leads to the same conclusion as the chi-square test for every service.

## R4b: Insight

**Insight.** Where members live does not change what they know about, or use, at the credit union. Awareness profiles are very similar in both groups, and no service shows a significant difference (all p ≥ .15; @tbl-r4b-chi). A few gaps look larger, but they are not reliable with groups this size. For example, more HQ-area members are unaware of the MasterCard (17.5% vs. 7.0%), yet the share who have used it is almost identical (43.9% vs. 43.7%; @tbl-r4b, @fig-r4b). The awareness problems found in R5, such as IRA loans and share collateralized loans, are shared by **all** members. They are not a result of living away from headquarters. Communication about services should therefore target the whole membership rather than one location.

## R4c: Cross-Tabulation & Chi-square Tests of Independence (Q11, Q12rc)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-xtab
#| tbl-cap: "Nominal operations items by residence (row % within each group)"

bind_rows(
  efcu |> count(residence, Answer = as.numeric(q11)) |>
    mutate(Item = "Q11: Statements easy to understand"),
  efcu |> filter(!is.na(q12rc)) |> count(residence, Answer = q12rc) |>
    mutate(Item = "Q12rc: Accounts kept confidential")
) |>
  group_by(Item, residence) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Answer = ifelse(Answer == 1, "Yes %", "No %")) |>
  select(Item, residence, Answer, pct) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Answer, values_from = pct) |>
  rename(Residence = residence) |>
```

```{r}

#| tbl-cap: "Chi-square tests of independence: nominal operations items by residence"

bind_rows(
  chi_row(efcu$q11,   efcu$residence, "Q11: Statements easy to understand"),
  chi_row(efcu$q12rc, efcu$residence, "Q12rc: Accounts kept confidential")
) |> kable()
```

## R4c: Insight

**Insight.** Members in both locations judge the credit union's operations about the same, with one exception: **the loan application**. Members in the headquarters area find loan applications *less* simple and easy (M = 3.28) than members elsewhere (M = 3.61). The difference is significant (Welch t(94.2) = −2.28, p = .025; @tbl-r4c-t). Only 49.1% of HQ-area members agree the forms are simple, compared with 64.8% elsewhere, and 21.1% of HQ-area members disagree, compared with 5.6% (@fig-r4c).

On every other measure, the two groups do not differ (all p > .10; @tbl-r4c-t, @tbl-r4c-chi). That includes statement frequency and accuracy, confidentiality, loan promptness, meeting needs, and overall management. HQ-area members are somewhat less likely to say their accounts are kept confidential (63.3% vs. 75.4%), but the difference is not significant (χ²(1) = 1.85, p = .173; @tbl-r4c-xtab, @tbl-r4c-chi).

The loan application was already the weakest item overall in R6. This result shows the problem is sharpest among the members who live closest to the credit union, so a simpler application should be tested with headquarters-area members first.

# Summary

## Key Takeaways

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of findings"

tibble(
  RQ = c("R3", "R6", "R4a", "R4b", "R4c"),
  Finding = c(
    "Employees are rated very highly (M = 4.21 of 5), especially for courtesy and helpfulness",
    "Operations rated highly overall; loan processes and statement frequency are the weak spots",
    "No difference in attitudes toward employees between HQ-area and other members",
    "No difference in awareness or use of any service between HQ-area and other members",
    "Groups agree on operations, except HQ-area members find loan applications less simple"),
  Implication = c(
    "Feature friendly, helpful staff as a reason to bank and borrow at the CU",
    "Simplify and speed up loan applications; review statement frequency",
    "Employee service is a strength for every member, wherever they live",
    "Raise awareness of lesser-known services across the whole membership",
    "Simplify the loan application, starting with headquarters-area members")
) |> kable()
```
